description: Mobile UI with a fixed 600px width banner causing horizontal page overflow scroll on a 390px mobile screen.
final_answer: The UI suffers from a critical responsiveness failure where a fixed-width blue banner (600px) exceeds the mobile viewport width (390px). This results in severe horizontal overflow, causing the right side of the banner and its internal text to be clipped. While the text paragraph below the banner is responsive and fits the screen, the banner itself breaks the layout flow and hides its right-side rounded corners, creating a broken and inconsistent user experience.
agreement_summary: Both the Expert and Skeptic judges agreed that the blue banner has a fixed width causing horizontal overflow and content truncation on the right edge of the mobile viewport.
decision_reason: The visual evidence is definitive: the banner's text explicitly states it is '600px wide' and is visibly cut off on the right side (e.g., 'viewpor' instead of 'viewport'). The Skeptic judge's additional observations regarding layout inconsistency and missing rounded corners are verified as direct consequences of the primary overflow issue.

issues.issue: Critical horizontal overflow and content truncation.
issues.evidence: The blue banner is clipped on the right edge, cutting off the heading '(Fixed' and the body text 'viewpor'. The text within the banner explicitly mentions it is 600px wide on a 390px viewport.
issues.probable_cause: A hard-coded 'width: 600px' CSS property applied to the banner container without a 'max-width: 100%' or responsive unit (like 'vw' or '%') to constrain it to the viewport.

issues.evidence: The 'Standard responsive text paragraph' correctly adheres to the viewport width, while the banner above it extends beyond the screen boundary, creating an asymmetrical layout.
issues.probable_cause: Inconsistent CSS application where the paragraph uses responsive layout rules while the banner uses fixed pixel dimensions.

issues.issue: Loss of visual affordance (clipped rounded corners).
issues.evidence: The right-side rounded corners of the blue banner are not visible because the element extends beyond the right edge of the screen.
issues.probable_cause: Overflow clipping caused by the fixed width of the element exceeding the viewport.
